title: Bacterial DNA Annotator: modular annotation and metabolic gap exploration for bacterial genomes
description:
Bacterial DNA Annotator is an open-source pipeline and web application for annotating bacterial genomes from scratch and exploring their metabolic gaps. It finds CDS, tRNA and rRNA, discovers unannotated ORFs, reconstructs metabolic networks, proposes operons and promoters, and presents the results in a clickable genome browser.

Every result declares its source, evidence, confidence and status. The graphical interface is available in Spanish, English and Simplified Chinese, runs on CPU, and includes a 150 kb demo genome. The 10 modules expose options, requirements, estimated time, status, self-test and execution; the ghost-gene module runs directly on an uploaded FASTA.

The public repository does not redistribute RegulonDB, KEGG, DoriC, STRING, DBTBS or BATTER data. The original code is MIT; third-party components keep their licenses.
